text:
Six blind men lived in a village. One day, a big elephant came to town. They wanted to know what an elephant is like. So each man touched the elephant.

The first man touched the side. “An elephant is like a wall!” he said.

The second man touched the tusk. “No, it’s like a spear!”

The third man held the trunk. “You are wrong! It’s like a snake!”

The fourth man touched the leg. “It’s like a tree!” he said.

The fifth man touched the ear. “No, it’s like a big fan!”

The sixth man held the tail. “It’s like a rope!” he said.

They began to argue. Each man thought he was right. They shouted for a long time.

A wise woman came and listened. “You are all right,” she said, “but you only touched one part. Put the parts together, and you will see the whole elephant.”

The men were quiet. They understood.

Moral: Everyone sees only a part of the truth. Listen to others.

quiz.q: There were six blind men in the story.
All the men touched the same part of the elephant.
What did the man who held the trunk say?
